# script: update: extend by git

Give the `update` script ([[DOT-277]]) a `git` target. **Motivation:** "`git pull` is not enough, sometimes I want to update submodules" — a project's dependencies can be git submodules tracking a branch, and bumping them means `submodule update --remote --merge`.

```bash
$ update git
#  - check __git
#  - git pull
#  - git submodule update --init --recursive --remote --merge
```

<!-- 2022-06-20T09:04Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/328#issuecomment-1160176467

instead of `update git` I extended `pull`.
-->

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/328#issuecomment-5711696729
Code vs intent: the ticket asked for an `update git` target; the fix commit instead added `--remote` to `pull`'s `git submodule update`. Consequence: every `pull` moves branch-tracking submodules to their remote tip, so repositories that pin submodules (including this one: `test/bats` etc.) get their pins silently advanced in the working tree — the dirty state `ensure_clean` then complains about.
-->
